(a) **Bilateral Element:** An electrical element whose properties (voltage-current relationship) are the same regardless of the direction of current flow through it. Example: Resistor, inductor, capacitor.

(b) **RMS Value of a Waveform:** The Root Mean Square (RMS) value is the effective value of an alternating quantity. It is defined as that steady DC current/voltage which produces the same amount of heat in a given resistance as is produced by the alternating quantity over a complete cycle.
$$I_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} i^2 dt}$$

(c) **Form Factor:** It is the ratio of the RMS value to the average value of an alternating waveform.
$$\text{Form Factor} = \frac{\text{RMS Value}}{\text{Average Value}}$$
For a pure sinusoidal wave, the form factor is always $\frac{1.11}{1} = 1.11$.
proTip: Form factor and peak factor are standard quality metrics of waveforms; remember the standard sine wave values: Form Factor = 1.11, Peak Factor = 1.414.
